# Picture credits and production briefings

Both illustrations were created for this prototype with the integrated imagegen tool. No real persons or historical documents. Production date: October 20, 2026. The files are in the project under `dist/assets/`.

- A-B01: `anna-schreibtisch.webp` – fictitious edition work; Old text and caption in the page.
- A-B02: `anna-mira.webp` – fictitious counterreading; Old text and caption in the page.
- A-B03 / A-G04: The technical detail is set as a real text comparison, not as an additional raster image. Thus the passage remains accessible, correctable and printable.

## Prompts actually used

### A-B01

Use case: illustrative-story. Asset type: editorial website opening illustration for a German scholarly edition case study. Create one warm sophisticated hand-painted gouache and pencil illustration, wide landscape 3:2. A researcher No legible text, no letters, no UI labels, no logos, no medieval cosplay, no heavy sepia, no infographic, no frame. This is fictional illustration, not historical evidence.

### A-B02

Use case: illustrative-story. Asset type: second editorial illustration for the same scholarly-edition website. Create one sophisticated warm hand-painted gouache and pencil illustration, landscape 3:2. Two women researchers are collaboratively comparing a short historical text passage at a table, seen mainly as two pairs of hands and partial shoulders, one points with a pencil to a sheet while the other holds a small open book. Two sheets with different understated blue and terracotta editorial markings, no readable text. Capture the detail of a useful question and careful collegial exchange. Ivory paper background, midnight teal, muted sage and terracasta affectible paper text. No faces required, no logos, no photorealism, no infographic, no frame. Fictional scene.

## Graphics

Work path, decision graph, matrix/coupling and edition comparison are built directly into HTML/CSS. You use the central rules in `engine.js`; no technical texts read from images.


## Addition of tool selection

Two more illustrations are in the same directory as `anna-tei.webp` and `anna-markdown.webp`. Their actual prompts and identification of fictitious program interfaces are in [werkzeug-bildnachweise.md](werkzeug-bildnachweise.md).
